attachments.origin_landmark: humeroulnar head: medial epicondyle + coronoid process (ulna_l); radial head: anterior oblique line of radius (radius_l)
attachments.insertion_landmark: middle phalanges, digits 2-5 (splits to allow FDP tendon to pass through, per digit)

actions: flexes PIP joints of digits 2-5 (prime mover)

functional_compartments.name: Index finger (digit 2) tendon slip
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: median n., muscular branch to FDS (index slip)

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: proximal-third endplate band of the index slip's belly

functional_compartments.function_note: Index slip's belly is the most independent/deepest, consistent with the index finger's greater independent motor control.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) (describes FDS as arising via humeroulnar and radial heads giving 4 tendons, with variable independence -- deepest for digit 2)

functional_compartments.name: Middle finger (digit 3) tendon slip
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: median n., muscular branch to FDS (middle slip)
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

functional_compartments.name: Ring finger (digit 4) tendon slip
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: median n., muscular branch to FDS (ring slip)
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

functional_compartments.name: Little finger (digit 5) tendon slip
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: median n., muscular branch to FDS (little finger slip, often thinnest)
functional_compartments.function_note: Often the smallest/most variable slip; least independent finger.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity musculoskeletal model (documents the 4 FDS tendon slips as functionally quasi-independent compartments)
